## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac.** 3-bets extremely wide (trash hands). Calls down light, barrels with air, turns weak hands into bluffs in single-raised pots. In 3-bet pots: stickier than expected — calls c-bets with middle pair, donk-bets when improving. Folds to 3-bets from tight players (P1, P5, P6). Against looser players' 3-bets (P4): sometimes calls with speculative hands. Gets it in preflop with QQ — standard for premiums. **Self-destructive over time — confirmed busting in Session 1 through overaggression.** Session 2: finished slightly below starting stack ($985). **Exploit**: 3-bet them liberally for value — they fold to tight images. Value bet thinner in single-raised pots. Do NOT bluff them in single-raised pots. Be patient — their aggression is eventually self-punishing.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, best player at table.** Opens and 4-bets as wide as TT (not just premiums), especially vs loose opponents. Calls opens with pocket pairs. Limps from SB with suited connectors/gappers. **Postflop trapping tendency**: On wet/monotone boards, checks draws on flop, then leads turn when completing draws. After making strong hands, checks river to induce bets and trap-calls. On dry boards, folds to aggression without connections. **Consistently finishes near starting stack** — patient accumulator who avoids big losses. **Exploit**: C-bet aggressively on dry boards. On wet boards, their checks do NOT mean weakness. When they lead turn after checking flop on draw-heavy boards, they likely completed a draw. Their river checks can be traps — don't value-bet thin. Avoid tangling without strong holdings.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~47%), passive preflop but open-raises stronger hands. Consistently accumulates chips — chip leader or near-top finisher across sessions despite station tendencies.** Limps weak holdings, open-raises better hands. Folds limps to raises. 3-bets with 99+. Folds 3-bet range to 4-bets. When already invested, EXTREMELY sticky — **confirmed calling river bets with 9-high and bottom pair. Will call down with virtually anything.** Check-raises when strongly connected (sets, strong top pair+). Otherwise just calls passively. Folds to c-bets on dry/missed boards. **More dangerous than pure station label suggests** — their calling habits let them realize equity and catch bluffs, which works when table over-bluffs. **Exploit**: Isolate limps with position. 4-bet lighter against their 99-QQ. C-bet dry boards. Value bet EXTREMELY wide — they call river with air. NEVER bluff them. Respect check-raises.

**Player 5**: **Ultra-nit preflop (~6% VPIP/PFR).** Any preflop raise/3-bet = extreme premium (AA/KK/QQ/AK). **Postflop: NOT weak-passive.** With made hands: donk-bets then folds to raises, calls one street then folds to turn barrels. With strong draws: donk-bets AND shoves. **Exploit**: Fold to their preflop aggression unless holding premiums. Two-barrel bluffs effective vs their made-hand range. Be cautious raising donk-bets on draw-heavy boards.

**Player 6**: **Tight for raises (~9%) BUT limping range is significantly wider.** Limps with hands as weak as K8o. 3-bets = QQ+/AK. Cold 4-bets = AA/KK. Flat-calls opens from blinds with sub-premium holdings (TT-JJ, AQ-type). Folds these flatting hands to subsequent 3-bets. **Postflop: Sticky/committed with premiums** — calls all-in with AK unimproved. **Exploit**: Fold to their 3-bets/4-bets unless premium. Isolate their limps freely. Do NOT bluff postflop. Squeeze over their blind flats.

**Player 7**: **Tight preflop but capable of 3-betting from position.** Defends BB/SB with pocket pairs and speculative hands. **As defender**: Peels flop/turn with marginal holdings but folds river without strong hands. Folds to flop check-raises. **As aggressor (checked to)**: Will stab/bluff rivers with air when sensing weakness. **Consistently loses chips across sessions ($755 end of S2)** — bleeds from calling two streets then folding, and from failed stabs. **Exploit**: Three-barrel bluffs effective when they're the caller. River bets from them after passive action = potentially a bluff. Isolate their BB. Their 3-bets may be wider than premium.

**Opponent Profiles & Tendencies:**
- **Player 1 (LAG / Spewy):** Highly aggressive and prone to overplaying. Opens extremely wide preflop (including offsuit K-high trash). Capable of massive multi-street bluffs with pure air, and will frequently take delayed stabs when flops check through. 
- **Player 2 (Extreme LAG / Calling Station):** Plays a very wide range (will open and call 3-bets OOP with medium suited gappers/connectors) and 3-bets light from the blinds. Post-flop, they are an absolute station—floats very light (e.g., check-calling with bottom pair) and capable of calling river shoves on scary boards with marginal hands. They barrel marginal hands on scary boards. *Exception:* In single-raised pots defending the Big Blind, they play straightforwardly and will fold to small c-bets on dry boards.
- **Player 4 (Aggressive / Extreme Station):** High VPIP/PFR but also capable of limping absolute garbage (e.g., 97o) from middle position. Crucially, their 3-bet range includes many non-premiums, and they will fold to 4-bets. Post-flop, they are capable of mind-boggling spew and station behavior—they will call turn bets with weak gutshots and even call river bets with absolute air (9-high). 
- **Player 5 (Passive / Recreational):** Classic limp/caller preflop, but will open-raise strong hands. Post-flop, they make probing donk-bets. *Crucial Note:* While some donk-bets are weak, they will play strong draws (like nut flush draws) extremely aggressively, donk-betting flops and open-shoving turns. Their preflop 3-bets represent an incredibly strong premium range.
- **Player 6 (Mixed TAG/Passive):** Previously thought to be tight, but they are capable of open-limping weak offsuit broadways (e.g., K8o) from early position. Their 3-bets still represent a very strong, value-heavy range (premiums and AK). Post-flop, they can be somewhat sticky, floating flop donk-bets with just AK-high, and will value bet two-pair hands on the river even on flush-completing boards.
- **Player 7 (Loose / Station):** Capable of overcalling post-flop with marginal made hands (e.g., underpairs with no draw) on scary or coordinated boards, even facing multiple opponents. Will also make small stabs/bluffs on the river with pure air when the action checks down.

**Strategic Adjustments & Exploits:**
- **Vs. Player 1:** Widen your bluff-catching range. Do not over-fold to their post-flop aggression; be prepared to call down with marginal made hands, especially when they stab at pots that check through.
- **Vs. Player 2:** NEVER bluff post-flop. Value bet relentlessly and go for maximum value (including overbets/shoves) even on scary runouts. Do not rely on flop check-raises as bluffs, as they float very wide. In blind-vs-blind or late-position steals, small c-bets on dry boards are highly profitable.
- **Vs. Player 4:** NEVER bluff them post-flop. They will call down with literal air. Value bet them relentlessly and thinly. Preflop, target them with isolation raises when they limp, and exploit their wide 3-betting range by 4-betting them (for value and as a bluff), as they will fold their non-premiums. 
- **Vs. Player 5:** Be cautious when raising their flop donk-bets on draw-heavy boards, as they are capable of shoving over the top with strong draws. Over-fold to their preflop 3-bets.
- **Vs. Player 6:** Give immense respect to their preflop aggression (3-bets), but realize their limping range is much wider and weaker than expected. You can isolate their limps wider. 
- **Vs. Player 7:** Value bet thinly and avoid bluffing, as they will call down with weak, marginal holdings. Can bluff-catch their small river stabs if the hand checks down.
